title: NetworkX double_edge_swap / random_reference: count rejected swaps so the null model is uniform
summary: The NetworkX chains only count successful swaps, or stop at the first success. Their exact stationary laws are proportional to the number of valid swaps (TV up to 0.078 from uniform, max/min ratio up to 2.5 on n<=7), and chi-square tests on the real code confirm this. A drafted, tested patch adds count_rejected to double_edge_swap and makes random_reference count every attempt; exact kernels after the patch are symmetric and uniform. The practical effect on real graphs is at most 0.03 null-SD, so this is a correctness and guarantee fix, not a result-changing one.

targets.name: networkx random_reference (break at first success, L115)

beneficiaries: NetworkX users computing degree-preserving null models: normalized rich-club (on by default), small-world sigma/omega, motif and assortativity z-scores
first_step: A human contributor searches NetworkX issues for prior reports (not possible from this session), opens an issue in their own words with the 13-realization reproduction and AI-use disclosure, then submits PR 1: keyword-only count_rejected plus docs.
measurement: Exact-enumeration unit test on d=[4,4,2,2,2,2] (13 realizations): max/min frequency ratio 2.0 before, 1.08 after. Exact kernel TV=0 after the patch on 5 sequences. Report null-mean shifts on standard graphs (<=0.03 SD).
risks: Maintainers may judge the bias negligible. The random_reference change alters seeded outputs and the effective swaps per niter. Under count_rejected, dense graphs need more attempts. Rich-club normalization changes break a seed-dependent test.

title: graph-tool random_rewire(persist=True): non-uniform law and infinite loop on unswitchable edges
summary: With persist=True, graph-tool retries the same edge until it succeeds. The exact stationary law is non-uniform (TV 0.039-0.054), confirmed on the real code (p=4e-254 vs uniform, p=0.80 vs the predicted law). The call never returns on any graph that has an edge with no valid switch partner, e.g. every graph with a vertex adjacent to all others, which includes every ego network; this was reproduced on a 30-vertex graph. The default persist=False is exactly uniform.

targets.name: graph-tool 2.98 source tarball (graph_rewiring.hh L276-L354 loop, L339-L343 persist; __init__.py L618-L623 docstring)

beneficiaries: graph-tool users who enable persist=True, which the docs say 'may improve the quality of the shuffling'
first_step: File an upstream issue with gt_persist_hub.py (hang) and the exact TV table. Propose documenting non-uniformity, capping retries, or deprecating persist for the configuration model.
measurement: The hang reproduction terminates. Exact or chi-square uniformity on the small sequences.
risks: The option is rarely used. The upstream git host is not reachable from this session, so a maintainer may already have changed it after 2.98.

title: Certify uniform-law samplers (igraph rewire, NetworKit EdgeSwitching/Curveball, graph-tool) with 131's explicit gap; certified budgets only for small graphs and Curveball
summary: 131's Lean-checked inequalities give explicit gaps for the edge-pair chains people run. They are Var<=2n^2<f,Lf>, which gives gap >= c/(2n^2), and Var<=<f,Hf>, which gives undirected random-pair Curveball gap >= 1/C(n,2). A Johnson-gap sharpening (H<=L, checked numerically on 8 instances, proof not yet written) removes the factor 2n^2. These justify docs that say 'mixes in polynomial time for every degree sequence'. Certified budgets are practical only for m up to a few hundred, or for Curveball burn-in up to n~1000; at m>=1e4 they are 1e6-1e20 times the 10m-100m defaults and say nothing about them.
beneficiaries: Network-science users of configuration-model nulls; library maintainers writing docs
first_step: Write a two-page note: the gap corollaries for edge-pair and Curveball chains, a proof of the sharpened H<=L via Johnson-scheme eigenvalues, and a budget table. Offer doc paragraphs to igraph and NetworKit.
measurement: Exact gaps against bounds on enumerable instances (paper constant 380-1500x loose; sharpened 5-12x; Curveball 3-5x). Wall-clock of certified budgets.
risks: Readers may treat certified worst-case budgets as recommended defaults. The theorem does not cover connected, directed or multigraph variants or GlobalCurveball. The sharpened constant needs a written proof.

title: vegan curveball: certified burn-in/thinning rule (FQW26 gap 1/C(r,2), key lemma Lean-checked via 131); quasiswap default thin
summary: vegan's curveball is exactly the row-pair heat bath analysed by Fu-Qin-Wang 2026 (gap >= 1/C(r,2)); exact gaps on 7 margin pairs respect the bound. A certified burn-in of C(r,2)(0.5 log|Omega|+log 2) trades and thin of C(r,2) ln(1/rho) cost milliseconds on typical site-by-species matrices. On sipoo they cut the run-to-run SD of oecosimu NODF z-scores from 1.05 (defaults burnin=0, thin=1) to 0.16. Separately, quasiswap with default thin=1 is non-uniform (TV up to 0.072) and becomes uniform with thin=100.
beneficiaries: Community ecologists running nestedness and co-occurrence null-model tests (oecosimu, permatswap)
first_step: Open a vegan issue proposing a certified burn-in helper for curveball, with the sipoo z-score stability table, and raising the default thin for quasiswap.
measurement: Run-to-run SD of z-scores under default vs certified settings on vegan's example datasets; exact TV of quasiswap at thin=1/10/100.
risks: FQW26 is an unrefereed AI-generated preprint; only its three-row lemma is Lean-checked (via 131). The bound covers row-pair trades only. Maintainers may prefer user-side diagnostics.

title: bctpy randmio_und: stop-at-first-success swap loop is non-uniform
summary: bctpy's randmio_und (a port of BCT) uses the same up-to-K-attempts-then-break pattern as NetworkX random_reference. The real code rejects uniformity (p=5e-34) and matches the predicted law. The fix is to count every attempt. Brain-network studies use it for small-world and rich-club nulls.
beneficiaries: Connectomics users of BCT/bctpy null models
first_step: Check the MATLAB BCT randmio_und.m for the same pattern, then file reports with the reproduction.
measurement: Chi-square uniformity on d=(4,4,2,2,2,2) before and after.
risks: The effect on real brain graphs is likely as small as for NetworkX (<=0.03 SD). bctpy maintenance activity is uncertain.

title: NetworkX is_regular_expander: nondeterministic on boundary spectra; bipartite always False; exact fallback only near the threshold
summary: The float eigsh test returns different answers for the same graph when a nontrivial eigenvalue equals +-2sqrt(d-1): C8 True in 13 of 30 calls, Petersen x C4 True in 2 of 40 relabelings. It always returns False for bipartite graphs because it compares against min(lams)=-d. 178's exact rational inertia test fixes the boundary case but costs 244 s at n=400 (float: 0.02 s), so it is useful only as a fallback when the float value is within a tolerance band of the threshold.
beneficiaries: Few: users testing structured or symmetric graphs for the Ramanujan property
first_step: Small issue: document the definition used (nonbipartite vs bipartite Ramanujan), handle -d for bipartite graphs, and add an exact integer fallback when |float lambda - 2sqrt(d-1)| < tol.
measurement: Deterministic answers on C8, Petersen x C4, Heawood and K33; no slowdown on random graphs.
risks: Low value: random samples essentially never land on the boundary. The full exact mode is O(n^4)-ish in big integers.

title: R igraph keeping_degseq default niter=100 total trials is far too small (independent of the papers)
summary: R igraph's keeping_degseq() defaults to 100 rewiring trials in total, whatever the graph size, while python-igraph and the C degree_sequence_game use 10m. On BA(2000) and power-law(2000) graphs, 95-98% of original edges survive against about 1-2% at stationarity. Not a consequence of 131, but found in the same audit.
beneficiaries: R igraph users calling rewire(g, keeping_degseq())
first_step: Check the rigraph issue tracker (a 2024 tool comparison already flagged the low trial count), then propose niter = 10*ecount(graph) or a warning.
measurement: Edge-overlap with the original graph after a default call, against the stationary value.
risks: May already be known or deliberately kept for backward compatibility.

title: Use 131's mixing bounds to set default swap counts (e.g. replace 10m/100m)
summary: Converted to swap counts, the Lean-checked bounds need 4.9e14 attempts per edge (igraph-style) at m=1e4 and 9.5e22 at m=1e6. Even the sharpened constant needs 2.5e8 and 4.8e12 per edge. That is 1e6-1e20 times the 10m-100m heuristics. Worst-case bounds can neither justify nor refute the defaults; empirical diagnostics remain the practice.
first_step: None; say this explicitly in any docs that cite 131.
risks: Overclaiming would erode trust in the certification work.

title: Family 115 as a certificate or sampler for ecology/statistics contingency-table null models
summary: 115 analyses an auxiliary padded small-cell chain weighted by completion counts. It does not analyse the 2x2 swap, Diaconis-Gangolli or quasiswap chains people run, and its constants are galactic (T=d^200(k+b)^2, exact correction 2^{500db}, over 1e256 steps for a 2x2 table). Fisher-type tests need the hypergeometric law (r2dtable), not the uniform one, and vegan's count models also fix fill. The 0-1 (presence-absence) case is FQW26, not 115.
first_step: None. A research question remains open: does the padding/repair technique give a polynomial gap for the plain 2x2 +/-1 swap chain on integer tables?

title: Implement 131's exact uniform sampler, or 178's deterministic Ramanujan construction, or a general exact=True Ramanujan mode
summary: 131's exact sampler enumerates all 2^{C(n,2)} graphs on a rare branch and is polynomial only in expectation. 178's construction has unspecified n_0(d) and k_d with scales such as n^{2e-7}, and outputs no local neighbour oracle; sample-then-verify already succeeds with probability about 0.69. A general exact Ramanujan test costs 8 s at n=200 and 244 s at n=400, against milliseconds for the float test.
